prompt.title: Apache Beam / Dataflow pipeline scaffolder and fusion/coder auditor

variables.var: SCAFFOLD a new pipeline or AUDIT an existing one

var.name: pipeline_goal
var.example: Read order events from Kafka, 1-minute revenue per store, write to BigQuery; late data up to 10 min.

var.name: pipeline_source
var.example: (the pipeline's Java source, or 'none' in SCAFFOLD mode)

variables.var: the static auditor's findings, so you start from evidence

var.name: job_evidence
var.example: Dataflow job graph: stage F3 fused Create+ExpandFn+Enrich, 1 worker busy of 40; GBK hot key store-42

variables.var: job graph, step timings, worker metrics, errors

context.platform: Apache Beam Java SDK 2.77.0, DataflowRunner in production, DirectRunner in tests; Java 21.

instructions.step: In AUDIT mode, confirm or reject each static finding against the source and the job evidence, then look for what static analysis cannot see. In SCAFFOLD mode, design the transform graph first and show it as a list of named steps with their PCollection types and coders.

Fusion: find every expensive fan-out that follows a small or slow source and would be fused into one stage; break it with Redistribute.arbitrarily() or Reshuffle.viaRandomKey(), placed after the fan-out.

Coders: give every PCollection element type an explicit, efficient coder (a schema via @DefaultSchema, or Avro or Proto); keys of GroupByKey, Combine.perKey and stateful DoFns must have deterministic coders.
Keys and aggregation: replace GroupByKey-then-sum with Combine.perKey; for skewed keys use withHotKeyFanout; state the key cardinality you assume.
Windows and triggers: unbounded inputs get a window, a trigger, allowed lateness and an accumulation mode that match the late-data rule.
DoFn lifecycle and sinks: clients created in @Setup and closed in @Teardown, never fields that cannot serialize; sink writes idempotent or exactly-once (BigQuery Storage Write API mode stated).
Write DirectRunner tests with TestPipeline and PAssert, including a late-data case with TestStream, run them, and report.

invariants.inv: No expensive ParDo is fused behind a source that produces few elements; each fan-out over 100x is followed by a redistribution.
No SerializableCoder on any PCollection; every key coder is deterministic.
Every per-key aggregation is a Combine with a combiner, not a GroupByKey followed by a loop.
Every unbounded PCollection reaching a grouping has a non-global window or an explicit trigger, plus allowed lateness.
DoFns hold no non-serializable fields; external clients live in @Setup and @Teardown.
Every sink's delivery semantics (at-least-once or exactly-once) is stated and the downstream consumer tolerates it.

anti_goals.no: No guessing about the runner's plan: claims about fusion cite the job graph or say they are predictions to check.
No GlobalWindow with a default trigger on an unbounded source.
No side inputs that grow without bound (a multi-gigabyte View.asMap rebuilt every window).
No rewrite of the whole pipeline when the audit finds three local fixes.

output_contract.file: findings table: id, evidence (source line or job metric), invariant, fix, expected effect, how to measure
TestPipeline and PAssert tests, a TestStream late-data test
output_contract.report: Before and after: stage count, the coder of each grouped PCollection, and the test results.

verification.check: List each fan-out with its ratio and the redistribution after it.
The static auditor reports no BM02/BM03 finding; a test constructs the pipeline (GroupByKey rejects a non-deterministic key coder at construction).
The static auditor reports no BM04 finding.
The TestStream test delivers an on-time, a late-within-lateness and a too-late element and asserts the panes.
A DirectRunner test runs the pipeline end to end: a DoFn that cannot serialize passes construction and fails only at run().
The audit document states each sink's semantics and the consumer's dedup key.

prompt.task: Run the pipeline work in {{mode}} mode for the goal above, honouring every invariant, and deliver the files and report of the output contract.
